newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A slowing of Asia's previously abundant export growth is undermining overall economic growth across the region. The Asian Development Bank's annual 'Outlook' report predicts that economic growth in the Asian Pacific region will rise about 7.4 percent after 8.2 percent growth the previous year. Page 1.

The Commonwealth Bank's aggressive cutting of its interest rates is failing to capture a bigger home loan market share, with CBA's share of new loans only 24 percent after initial highs of 30 percent. In February, the CBA cut its standard variable homeloan rate to 7.55 percent from 8.25 percent but this has proved no guarantee of success. Page 1.

MIM Holdings Ltd has gained a majority stake in the Newlands-Collinsville-Abbot Point coal project, renewing its commitment to the Australian coal industry. A feasibility study has established the viability of the mine and will follow a new enterprise agreement and a strong profit period. Page 35.

Canadian brewer Molson Breweries has settled a four year dispute over licensing agreements with U.S. beer giant Coors, costing Foster's Brewing Group, with a 40 percent ownership of Molson's, at least $A34 million. Despite a payout of $A92 million, Molson retains the right to brew and distribute Coors products in Canada under a new arrangement. Page 35.

Australian National Industries has sold its German waste water treatment unit and will try to sell of the remainder of its loss-making European assets to close its disastrous Holter investment. The total sale of the waste-water treatment businss and a 50 percent stake in its Danish technology group was an abnormal profit of $A13 million. Page 35.

Cigarette group WD & HO Wills has told shareholders earnings for the financial year will increase with hopes of improving its market share above 30 percent before June 30. The company indicated it will not engage in a price war to increase market share but will continue to operate in a difficult environment, with $A1.2 billion paid in taxes to the federal government. Page 37.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The 1,640 km Dampier to Bunbury gas pipeline system in Western Australia will be on offer for privatisation at an estimated cost of up to A$1.5 billion. Selling the 100 percent stake, the Western Australia government has reversed its previously preferred option toretain a strategic 30 to 50 percent stake in the nation's biggest gas pipline. Page 23.

The demutualisation of the Australian Stock Exchange became a step closer yesterday after the federal government announced legislation would be introduced to facilitate the process. Under the draft bill, any individual investor would be restricted to a five percent stake in the ASX. Page 23.

WD & HO Wills Holdings Ltd chairman Nick Greiner yesterday moved to quell the market saying lawsuits pending against Australia's tobacco companies would not be affected by the rumoured settlement in the United States. Greiner dismissed claims as "speculatve" of Australian tobacco groups becoming involved in negotiations for compensation packages. Page 23.

The largest sale of Australian uranium has been finalised with WMC Ltd securing a long-term contract to supply uranium to Japanese power group Tokyo Electric Power Co in a deal estimated to be worth more than A$40 million a year. Page 23.

At a time which has been marked by a depressed market, Amcor Ltd will restructure its operations in a bid to slice up to A$30 million of costs as the paper and packaging producer re-focuses its management operations. The market has endorsed the move as Amcor's shares were pushed up 22 cents to A$8.23 yesterday. Page 25.

Advance Bank will launch Australia's first Internet banking facility despite a warning from Germany's central bank, the Bundesbank, that this may increase the possibility of fraud. The bank will launch a pilot program using selected staff and merchants in two weeks. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Mining giant BHP has decided to defer plans to expand to expand its copper business as it continues a major cost-cutting exercise aimed at better returns from its A$3.2 billion takeover of Magma Copper. BHP has signalled the planned expansion might not happen in the previously indicated timeframe as it seeks to improve Magma's short-term performance. Page 25.

Analysts at Rothschild Australia are anticipating next week's release of the March quarter inflation figures will show a marked decline and further falls can be expected throughout the year. Rothschild economists are predicting that the March figures will reveal deflation - a phenomenon not seen in Australia for five years. Page 25.

Building materials group Pioneer International is looking for expansion into India, Indonesia, and Europe in anticipation of its possible A$500 million-plus sale of its half-share in petrol refiner Ampol. Pioneer has indicated any possible purchase would be limited to building materials expansion. Page 25.

Tobacco major W.D. & H.O. Wills is looking to lift its market share to 30 percent this year in an action which could spark a renewed tobacco price war with rival Philip Morris. Meanwhile, Wills chairman Nick Greiner assured a shareholders meeting that recent legal developments involving the U.S. tobacco industry had no implications for Australian firms. Page 25.

A restructuring plan by packaging group Amcor is expected to save about A$30 million as job cuts and some executive changes are flagged. Amcor managing director Don Macfarlane has moved for a plan that will see an overhaul of the group's administration an business units. Page 27.

In an attempt to improve the efficiency and competitiveness of the Australian Stock Exchange, the federal government has indicated it will introduce legislation to pave the way for the demutualisation and eventual public listing of the ASX. The ASX has indicated that the process for the move be in place by next January. Page 30.
THE AGE

Optus Communications wants to undercut Telstra's own 25-cent local call in return for supporting to cut Telstra's pay TV costs. This deal will be an important part of a broader infrastructure deal being discussed while the companies continue to talk about reducing further overlap in their controversial aerial cable networks. Page B1.

Foster's Brewing Group and other partners in Molson Breweries will pay U.S. giant Coors Brewing $A93 million after the partners agreed to settle a dispute over the licensing and distribution of Coors' products in Canada. This has led to a formal partnership, known as Coors Canada, which will keep intact Foster's share of profits from the Canadian sales of Coors. Page B1.

The Newlands-Collinsville-Abbott Point coal project in Queensland will be expanded into one of Australia's biggest coal mines after MIM Holdings Ltd exercised its option to remain a 75 percent partner in the project under a deal with Itochu Corp. Production will rise from 4.5 million to seven million tonnes a year by the year 2000. Page B3.

Business on the sharemarket yesterday was dominated by dealing in two property investment stocks, Gandel Retail Trust and Countrywide Retail Trust, with combined trades totalling nearly $A50 million. Market watchers believe retail magnate John Gandel may have sold part of his substantial holding in the Trust, which finished the day one cent lower. Page B2.

WMC's expanded Olympic Dam copper-uranium mine in South Australia is likely to produce uranium at much higher rates than predicted. Annual uranium output will be 4,630 tonnes, up by 25 percent on the previously forecast 3,700 tonnes and higher than the present output of 1,500 tonnes. WMC announced yesterday it had won a 10-year contract to supply Tokyo Electric Power Company from 1999. Page B3.

A restructuring and overhaul of administration and business operations is expected to save Amcor about $A30 million. This has been forced upon Amcor by the sharp decline in profitability as world paper prices remain low and customers are seeking lower prices for packaged products. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
